summary.text: 休 is commonly read as a person resting beside a tree. A competing account sees military marker posts and associates the graph with recognition of merit; the original motivation remains disputed.

formation.text: The common analysis treats 休 as a semantic compound: 人 depicts a person and 木 depicts a tree, together forming a resting scene. Some early forms are interpreted as showing the tree top bending toward the person to suggest shade. A competing analysis reads the right-hand element as 禾-like marker posts at a military gate.

components.text: In the common analysis, 人 depicts the person in the scene. The competing account disputes the whole graph’s interpretation but does not offer a different account of this element.

In the common analysis, 木 depicts the tree; some early forms are interpreted as bending its top toward the person to suggest shade. This identification is disputed by the account that reads the element as 禾-like military marker posts.

history.text: Catalogs list 休 in oracle-bone and bronze examples and in the seal-script category, but these records do not establish a sequence of graphic changes.

The transmitted 說文 account defines 休 as “cease; rest” and explains it as a person relying on a tree. A competing account proposes paired marker posts at a military gate instead; the explanations disagree about the graph’s original motivation.

uncertainties.text: The person-and-tree and military marker-post interpretations disagree about the right-hand element and the graph’s original motivation; the accounts do not resolve the dispute.
The cited bronze and received-text uses have no securely established order here, so the earliest lexical sense cannot be ranked confidently.

senses.text: Rest is supported by received-text examples and the transmitted 說文 definition; the cited examples do not establish that it was the earliest attested sense.
休 is also used to mean “stop” or “cease.” The cited examples do not show when this use arose relative to “rest.”
One proposed connection links resting in shade with shelter or protection, but the cited uses do not establish that development or its chronology.
Reported inscriptional uses include favor or reward. Their relationship to rest or shelter remains uncertain.
A competing graph analysis cites a bronze use glossed “good” or “commendable” and connects it with recognition of merit. This use does not settle the graph’s origin or the sense’s chronology.
The common current meaning includes resting or taking a break.

developments.text: Both meanings are attested, but the cited evidence does not show that one developed from the other.

limitations.text: The earliest lexical sense cannot be ranked securely. Proposed connections among shade, protection, favor, reward, goodness, pleasure, rest, and stopping do not establish a proven sequence.

overview.text: 休 is commonly explained as a person resting beside a tree: 人 and 木 form the scene. Another interpretation reads the right side as military marker posts, so the graph’s original motivation remains uncertain.

components.text: 人 depicts the person in the common person-and-tree scene.
木 depicts the tree in the common analysis; the marker-post interpretation disputes this identification.

relationships.text: In the common person-and-tree interpretation, 人 depicts the person in the scene represented by 休.
In the common analysis, 木 depicts the tree beside which the person rests; the marker-post interpretation disputes this identification.
